Based on the initial blood work and X-ray results, does the swelling in your right knee involve pain during movement or at rest, and have you noticed any stiffness or locking sensations?

REQUEST TEST: Uric_Acid, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Knee_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text:
The uric acid, autoimmune markers, and ultrasound are all normal, which helps rule out gout, rheumatoid arthritis, and significant soft tissue tears. Since the issue appears to be mechanical or structural given your family history, has there been a specific injury to this knee, and do you feel a distinct popping sound when it swells?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Knee
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Knee

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal MRI results effectively rule out meniscal tears, ligament ruptures, and fractures, which aligns with your negative history of specific trauma. Given your persistent swelling and strong family history of similar issues, do you notice any warmth, redness, or a sensation of the knee "giving way" when you walk?

REQUEST TEST: Knee_Joint_Aspiration_Analysis (for crystals and cell count)
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Knee_MRI

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor

Since all imaging, blood work, and joint aspiration have returned normal results, ruling out infection, crystals, and structural damage, I need to clarify your specific activity patterns: does the swelling consistently occur after prolonged standing or walking, and does it subside when you elevate your leg?
